questions.question: A hundredths grid is one whole (100%) split into 100 equal squares. Every square is blank except one, and that one square is cut in half with only one half coloured in. What percent of the grid is coloured?
questions.explain: One square is one hundredth of the grid, which is 1%, so half of a square is half of 1%, that is 0.5%. The common trap is thinking percents stop at 1%, or reading 'half' as half of the whole grid.

questions.question: Two hundredths grids sit side by side. Each grid has 100 equal squares, and each whole grid stands for 100%. On the first grid all 100 squares are shaded; on the second grid 25 squares are shaded. Using one grid as the whole, what percent is shaded altogether?
questions.explain: Each full grid is 100%, so one whole grid plus 25 more squares is 100% + 25% = 125%. The trap is treating the two grids together as the whole, which turns 125 shaded squares into 62.5%.

questions.question: On a hundredths grid of 100 equal squares the whole grid is 100%. Each square is then cut into 4 equal small pieces. Exactly 3 small pieces are shaded and nothing else. What percent of the grid is shaded?
options: 3%, one percent for each shaded part
questions.explain: Each square is 1%, so a quarter of a square is 0.25%, and 3 of those quarters make 0.75%. The trap is counting the 3 shaded pieces as 3%, but the pieces are smaller than whole squares.

questions.question: Each hundredths grid has 100 equal squares and stands for one whole, or 100%. Kai wants to shade exactly 250% using blank grids. What should Kai shade?
options: Only one whole grid, since 100% is the top
Two whole grids and half of one more square
250 whole grids, one grid for each percent
Two whole grids and 50 squares of a third
questions.explain: 250% is two whole grids (200%) plus 50 more squares, because each square is 1% and half a grid is 50%. The trap is believing 100% is the maximum, or shading one grid per percent.

questions.question: Which decimal has exactly the same value as 0.4%?
options: no decimal fits a percent under 1%
questions.explain: Percent means hundredths, so 0.4% is 0.4 out of 100, and 0.4 divided by 100 is 0.004. The trap is dropping the percent sign and writing 0.4, which really means 40%.

questions.question: Which of these has exactly the same value as 175%?
questions.explain: 175% means 175 hundredths, so 175 divided by 100 is 1.75, which is more than one whole. The trap is keeping 175 as a plain number; a percent is always compared with 100.

questions.question: A Surrey secondary school has 1000 students. Exactly 0.2% of the students are on the chess team. How many students is that?
questions.explain: 0.2% means 0.2 out of every 100, and 1000 students is ten groups of 100, so ten lots of 0.2 gives 2 students. The trap is reading 0.2% as 2%, or using 0.2 as if it were the answer itself.

questions.question: In April, Ravi's sunflower was 20 cm tall. In June the same sunflower measured 300% of its April height. How tall was the sunflower in June?
options: 80 cm, April's height plus 300% of it
300 cm, the percent used as the number
questions.explain: 100% is the whole 20 cm, so 300% is three times 20 cm, which is 60 cm. The trap is copying 300 down as a measurement, or treating 300% of as if it meant an increase of 300%.

questions.question: Last month Jasmine's class sold 40 boxes of cookies for a Grade 8 trip. This month they sold 140% of last month's amount. How many more boxes did they sell this month than last month?
options: 56 more boxes, all of this month's boxes
140 more boxes, one for each percent
0 more boxes, since 100% is the top
questions.explain: 140% of 40 is 1.4 times 40, which is 56 boxes, and the question asks how many more, so 56 − 40 = 16. The trap is stopping at 56, which is this month's total rather than the increase.

questions.question: A Victoria school club raises $4000 through a donation website. The website keeps 0.5% of the money as a fee, and the club keeps the rest. How much money does the club keep?
options: $2000 left, since half is the fee
questions.explain: 1% of $4000 is $40, and 0.5% is half of that, so the fee is $20 and the club keeps $4000 − $20 = $3980. The trap is reading 0.5% as 5%, or as one half of the whole amount.

questions.question: A shop sign says a new bike costs 120% of last year's price. Priya says the sign must be wrong because nothing can be more than 100%. What is the best reply?
options: Priya is right, 120 is just a number
Priya is right, 100% is the largest
questions.explain: Percents above 100% simply mean more than one whole, so 120% is 1.2 times last year's price, the original amount plus a fifth of it. The trap is treating 100% as a ceiling instead of as one whole.

questions.question: Tia shades half of one square on a 100-square hundredths grid and labels the shading 0.5%. Nate says you cannot shade less than one whole square, so the label must be 1%. Who is correct?
options: Nate is right, 1% is the smallest percent
Neither, half a square is 0.5, not 0.5%
Nate is right, half a square rounds to 1%
Tia is right, half a hundredth is 0.5%
questions.explain: One square is one hundredth, or 1%, so half of that square is 0.5%, showing that percents can be smaller than 1%. The trap is rounding up to a whole square, or writing 0.5 as if the percent sign did not change its meaning.
